description.value: The study investigated relationships between Social Cognition and Emotional Assessment subtest performance and regional gray matter volume in patients with behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia using voxel-based morphometry.

spans.text: we investigated the relationship between performance on the SEA subtests (including the mini-SEA) and regional gray matter volume in patients with bvFTD using voxel-based morphometry (VBM)

description.value: The SEA is a battery composed of five different subtests: a theory of mind evaluation (Faux-Pas test), a facial emotion recognition test, reversal-learning and behavioral-control tests, and an apathy scale.

spans.text: neuropsychological battery
Faux-Pas test
theory of mind evaluation

description.value: A 10-story short version of the Faux-Pas test used to evaluate theory of mind. The study calculated a detection-of-faux-pas score and an explanation-of-faux-pas score, with the latter requiring identification of what the faux pas was, who made it, why it occurred, whether it was intentional, and how the victim felt. It was administered as one of the SEA subtests to characterize social-cognitive impairment and for the VBM analysis.

spans.text: We used a short (10 stories) version of the Faux-Pas test (Stone, Baron-Cohen, & Knight, Reference Stone, Baron-Cohen and Knight1998) to evaluate theory of mind. For this study, we calculated two scores: a “detection of faux-pas” score and an “explanation of faux-pas” score (What was the faux-pas? Who made it? Why? Was it intentional? How did the victim feel?).
Reversal-learning task
Reversal-learning task

description.value: A reversal-learning task adapted from Rolls et al. in which participants learned which item was advantageously rewarded, then faced unexpected reversal of the reward contingencies and finally an extinction phase. The study recorded the number of trials needed to pass the reversal phase (reversal score), number of reversals (global reversal score), and errors before reversing the first rule (reversal errors). It was administered to characterize affective shifting/reinforcement-learning impairment and for the VBM analysis.

spans.text: This test had been adapted from the original paradigm of Rolls et al. (Reference Rolls, Hornak, Wade and McGrath1994) and included three phases.
Behavioral-control test
Behavioral-control test

description.value: A behavioral-control task requiring participants to choose between two items under virtual monetary reward or punishment while discovering and following three successive rules: alternating items, choosing the first item on every trial, and choosing the second item on every trial. The study scored errors before reaching the second rule, termed reversal errors, and also analyzed a reversal score. It was administered as an SEA subtest to characterize behavioral control and for the VBM analysis.

spans.text: In this test, the patients had to choose between two items on the basis of a virtual monetary reward or punishment. Three consecutive rules were to be found and followed. First, an alternation between the two items was required. Second, the patients had to choose the first item at each trial. Finally, the second item had to be chosen at each trial.
Facial emotions recognition test
emotion recognition test

description.value: A facial emotion recognition test presenting 35 Ekman faces. Participants identified the expressed emotion from fear, sadness, disgust, surprise, anger, happiness, or neutral. The outcome was the percentage of accurately recognized emotions. It was administered to characterize emotional-processing impairment and for the VBM analysis.

spans.text: Thirty-five faces from Ekman pictures (Ekman & Friesen, Reference Ekman and Friesen1975) were presented.

clinical scale

description.value: A caregiver-rated questionnaire adapted from Starkstein's Apathy Scale, used to assess the severity of apathetic symptoms. The resulting apathy scale score was entered as a covariate in the VBM analysis.

spans.text: Apathy was assessed by caregivers using a questionnaire adapted from Starkstein (the “Apathy Scale”) (Starkstein et al., Reference Starkstein, Mayberg, Preziosi, Andrezejewski, Leiguarda and Robinson1992).
All patients underwent the same imaging protocol with whole-brain T1 images using a 1.5 Tesla GE-Medical System MRI scanner.

spans.text: The bvFTD patients were enrolled according to the Lund and Manchester criteria for bvFTD diagnosis (Neary et al., Reference Neary, Snowden, Gustafson, Passant, Stuss, Black and Benson1998) and fulfilled the recently revised diagnostic criteria (Rascovsky et al., Reference Rascovsky, Hodges, Knopman, Mendez, Kramer, Neuhaus and Miller2011).

spans.text: Patients were excluded if they presented any of the following: (1) language complaints (progressive non-fluent aphasia or semantic dementia); (2) systemic illnesses that could interfere with cognitive functioning; (3) vascular lesions seen on MRI or neurological history suggestive of vascular dementia; (4) motor-neuron disease; (5) major depression; or (6) use of anxiolytics or antipsychotics drugs.
